packages.docs:
Host-mediated action bus for Spores.

A Spore sees a granted action catalog and emits bounded invocations. The host
owns grants, approval, idempotency, credentials, routing, retries and audit.
Unibus adapters implement the actions; Spores never import Unibus or open a
connector-specific transport.

interfaces.docs:
Presentation projection of the granted action catalog.

This never grants execution. A caller may render a button or parameter form
from this data, then invoke through `actions.invoke`.
interfaces.name: catalog

packages.name: actions

packages.docs:
Host-attested context for an incoming HTTP invocation.

The host owns the listener, TLS, and routing. A Spore sees the request only
through `wasi:http`; this interface adds the host-side facts that must not be
spoofable request headers: which Spore ran, which route grant matched, and
who is on the other end of the transport.

`current` is valid only for the duration of one `incoming-handler` call. A
host that calls a component outside an HTTP invocation has no context to
report and fails the call rather than inventing one.
packages.name: http-context

packages.docs:
Hook administration: the one door the CLI and a console both use.

This is a product contract, not a runtime one (`fungos:`, not `soil:`): only a
webhook product knows what a slug, a provider and a tenant are. The host
implements it because the host owns the registry and, later, Geode - a guest
that can create a hook is not a guest that should be able to read the secret
bytes behind one.

The secret crosses this boundary exactly once, in `created`. There is no
read, no export and no list-of-secrets: a hook that is lost is revoked and
made again, which is cheaper than a capability that hands out credentials.

functions.docs:
Register a hook and mint its credential.

One call, not two: a hook without a credential accepts nothing, and a
credential without a hook is a secret nobody owns.
functions.name: create

functions.docs: Every hook the caller may see. Never includes secrets.
functions.name: hooks

functions.docs:
Revoke a hook and its credential. `false` means it was already gone,
which is not an error - the caller wanted it absent and it is absent.
functions.name: revoke

types.docs: The only value that ever carries a secret.
types.name: created

types.docs: A registered endpoint. The secret is deliberately absent.
types.name: hook

packages.name: webhooks

packages.docs:
Private app storage.

AppData is scoped to the signed Spore's app identity and the current user.
The Spore sees opaque keys and bytes, never a host path, table, app id, or
another app's namespace.

`local` is device-only. `synced` is a per-app, per-user private book that
replicates through the native records engine. Synced AppData is not indexed
or shareable; structured/shareable data belongs in `soil:records`.

functions.docs: List metadata for keys under a prefix. Values are fetched separately.
functions.name: [method]store.list-keys

functions.docs: Last-writer-wins per key. Returns the new generation.
functions.name: [method]store.set

functions.docs: Compare-and-set against the caller's last observed generation.
functions.name: [method]store.set-if-generation

packages.name: appdata

packages.docs:
Host BLE radio capability.

Transport stays in Soil; the device protocol stays in the Spore. A Spore
receives Soil-issued device handles and characteristic UUIDs, never a MAC,
path, socket, permission, or radio handle it can forge.

Limits (Soil-enforced, not expressible in WIT):
- at most 64 devices per scan, 8 subscribed characteristics per link
- scan <= 30 s; next-event bounded per call; every call has a deadline
- read <= 512 B per call; write <= 512 B per call; the Spore chunks frames
- at most one link and one live radio lease per Soil host
- no fs, net, clock, env, or device enumeration beyond scan results

functions.docs: Connect to a previously scanned handle. The host takes the radio lease.
functions.name: connect

functions.docs:
Wait up to `timeout-ms` for one event; `none` means the deadline expired
and is not an error.
functions.name: next-event

functions.docs: Read at most `max-bytes` from a characteristic. `0` is `invalid`.
functions.name: read

functions.docs: Active scan for `timeout-ms`, returning Soil-issued handles.
functions.name: scan

functions.docs: Discovered GATT tree on the current link.
functions.name: services

functions.docs:
Enable notifications for a characteristic. Events are drained with
`next-event`.
functions.name: subscribe

types.docs: Soil-issued handle for a scan result. Opaque; not an address.
types.name: device-handle

types.docs: One inbound radio event.
types.name: event

types.docs:
One inbound notification. The UUID lets a Spore tell the command channel
from DFU; the payload is still opaque.
types.name: notification

packages.name: ble

packages.docs:
Canvas is the cross-platform owner: window, compositor, layout, theme,
rendering and input lifecycle stay in the host. A Spore is logic/data and
asks the granted Canvas surface to present or to receive normalized input.

Limits (host-enforced):
- one granted surface per Spore; the host selects extent and display
- one present and one input per invocation; no per-frame callback
- input is a bounded semantic key or one printable Unicode scalar, never a
  raw keycode, scan code or device event
- no pixels, framebuffer, DRM handle, window handle, path or clock

functions.docs: Release the grant. Further calls return `closed`.
functions.name: close

functions.docs:
Deliver one normalized event. `generation` must match the state the
caller last observed; a stale generation is refused, never reordered.
Text arrives as `character`; raw keycodes and platform scan codes never
cross this boundary.
functions.name: input

functions.docs: Read the current owner state without presenting.
functions.name: observe

functions.docs:
Present into the space the host granted.

`document` is a versioned payload from `soil-scene`: a scene the host
rasterizes, an RGBA frame the Spore rendered, or a lease on a GPU texture.
It is bytes rather than a WIT type on purpose -- a new node kind must not
rebuild every Spore that draws. The host validates it and refuses anything
it cannot present, naming the reason.
functions.name: present

types.docs:
Theme tokens the host has already resolved. A Spore-owned renderer reads
these instead of guessing colors from a screenshot or hard-coding its own.
types.name: theme

packages.name: canvas

packages.docs:
Host-mediated credentials.

A Spore names a credential and asks the host to sign or verify. Secret bytes
never enter the guest: `resolve` returns an opaque handle, and every
operation is re-checked against the host's grant and expiry on use.

The host adapter for this interface is Geode (Mycelium). This contract is
deliberately smaller than a key store: no enumeration, no read, no export.

functions.docs: Resolve a granted credential name to an opaque handle.
functions.name: resolve

functions.docs: Sign a message with a resolved handle.
functions.name: sign

functions.docs:
Verify a signature with a resolved handle. A mismatched signature is
`ok(false)`, not an error; errors describe the credential or request.
functions.name: verify

packages.name: creds

packages.docs:
Semantic device capabilities.

Runtime uses the documented bounded core-Wasm lowering, not component
canonical ABI. Battery is measured, estimate is model output, and lid is a
read-only switch observation. Grants remain per interface.

interfaces.docs:
Semantic interface. Runtime uses the documented core-Wasm lowering, not
component canonical ABI. Tokens are invocation-scoped, single-use handles.
interfaces.name: battery

interfaces.docs:
Model output, never measured SOC or kernel battery capacity. Runtime uses
the documented bounded core-Wasm lowering, not component canonical ABI.
interfaces.name: estimate

interfaces.docs:
Read-only lid capability. Host grants permission per guest; never grants
raw device access, socket selection, display policy or input injection.

functions.docs:
Bounded diagnostic: guest requests logging its most recent read.
Not arbitrary text and not device/display authority.
functions.name: log-change

interfaces.name: lid

packages.name: device

packages.docs:
Read-only graph queries over explicit record links and references.

The graph is derived from records in host-approved books. A node or edge is
a locator; this contract never grants access to the target.

functions.docs: Query edges attached to `node`. Empty `rel` means every relationship.
functions.name: neighbors

functions.docs: Query external identifiers attached to `node`.
functions.name: references

packages.name: graph

packages.docs:
Bounded host-mediated HTTP.

The guest names an absolute URL and an optional host-resolved credential
handle. The host checks its origin allowlist, injects the credential, refuses
unbounded bodies and redirects, and returns one bounded response. Raw sockets,
DNS control, proxy configuration and secret bytes never cross this boundary.
packages.name: http

packages.docs:
Derived, rebuildable index over the VFS namespace.

The index is not authority. It never creates, mutates or owns a file; it
answers browse/search queries and returns paths. The Spore then calls
`soil:vfs.stat`/`read` for the authoritative entry and bytes. A host may
rebuild the index at any time and bump `generation`.

functions.docs: Browse direct children in the requested order.
functions.name: browse

functions.docs:
Exact KNN over the host embedding index. Returns `unsupported` when the
host has no embedding provider; guests never choose a model.
functions.name: knn

functions.docs:
Rebuild from the current VFS namespace. Hosts may also rebuild in the
background; this call is the explicit refresh boundary.
functions.name: refresh

functions.docs:
Search paths, media types, metadata, and indexed text. Results are paths;
call `soil:vfs.stat` for authoritative entry data.
functions.name: search

functions.docs: Inspect index readiness and generation.
functions.name: state

packages.name: index

packages.docs:
Host-mediated language-model inference.

The host owns provider selection, endpoint discovery, authentication, model
aliases, budgets, and transport. A Spore names a model, messages, and tools.
Credentials and provider routes never cross this boundary.

functions.docs: Read the next chunk. `none` means the timeout elapsed without data.
functions.name: [method]completion-stream.next

functions.docs: Non-streaming completion.
functions.name: complete

functions.docs: List models visible to this host/profile.
functions.name: models

functions.docs:
Open a streaming completion. The returned resource is bounded by the host
session and must be cancelled or dropped when the guest is done.
functions.name: open-stream

types.docs: Streaming response handle. The guest polls it at its own cadence.
types.name: completion-stream

packages.name: inference

packages.docs:
Shared normalized input types.

Presentation surfaces (Canvas, Terminal, imported surfaces) use the same
semantic key, pointer, scroll and text vocabulary. The host owns platform
keycode and IME translation; guests only see these normalized values.

types.docs:
Host-normalized key. `named` is an escape hatch for imported native
surfaces that expose stable semantic names the host cannot map further.
types.name: key

types.docs: Normalized surface coordinates, 0..=1.
types.name: point

packages.name: input

packages.docs:
Host-mediated media sources.

A Spore names a host-reviewed source id. It never receives a URL, Unibus
peer, API token, decoder handle, or raw socket. Playback is decoded and
presented by the host; encoded access is a separate grant.

types.docs:
Explicit encoded access for recording, remuxing, transcoding, inspection,
or a codec the host cannot present. Not implied by playback.
types.name: encoded-stream

types.docs:
One decoded image. The host may downsample to satisfy the requested
bounds; the returned dimensions are authoritative.
types.name: image

types.docs:
Host-owned playback. The host owns demuxing, decode, A/V clock, audio
device, and presentation surface.
types.name: playback

packages.name: media

packages.docs:
Mycelium-backed directory and terminal session capability.

The host owns identity, certificates, routing, jump hosts, host-key
verification and the SSH profile. A Spore names an opaque target id obtained
from `directory`; it never supplies a host, port, credential or private key.

The handles below are component-instance-scoped and unforgeable in the sense
that the host only accepts handles it issued. A later revision can replace
them with WIT resources without changing the verbs.

functions.docs: Fetch one visible target without listing.
functions.name: get

functions.docs: List visible targets. `kind` is a display filter, not authority.
functions.name: targets

functions.docs: Run a non-interactive command for agents. No PTY, no VT semantics.
functions.name: exec

functions.docs:
Open an interactive PTY shell through the host's Mycelium SSH profile.
`cols` and `rows` seed the remote terminal size.
functions.name: open-shell

functions.docs:
Read bytes from the PTY. Empty list means the timeout elapsed; `none`
means the session reached EOF.
functions.name: read

functions.docs: Tell the remote PTY its new window size.
functions.name: resize

functions.docs: Write input bytes to the PTY.
functions.name: write

packages.name: mycelium

packages.docs:
Host-mediated notifications, focus, history and cleanup.

A publisher emits a durable notification envelope. An inbox shows and acts on
it. Focus is a host-owned per-device policy; history is opt-in and separately
granted. No payload carries app identity, a URL, a credential or authority.
packages.name: notify

packages.docs:
Host-attested principal identity.

Mycelium identity / OIDC is the source of truth. The host verifies the
token or device identity and exposes only this minimal projection. Tokens,
refresh credentials, raw claims and private keys never cross the boundary.

A principal answers "who". It does not grant access; exact WIT grants and
book grants still decide what the caller may do and where.
packages.name: principal

packages.docs:
Durable, schema-tagged records with a change feed and peer sync.

Records are the storage layer for Spores that need queryable state (mail and
chat metadata, contacts, CRM snapshots) without inventing a second database.
The host owns durability, revisions, tombstones, and sync. A Spore owns the
schema and the meaning of `body`.

Grants are separate: read, write, and sync. A read-only Spore cannot mutate
or export the store.

functions.docs:
Merge remote changes with last-writer-wins. This never calls back into
the network; the Spore or host transports the page.
functions.name: apply

functions.docs:
Export changes after `since`, ordered by `(revision, origin)`. This is the
sync producer side; pass the result to `apply` on the peer.
functions.name: changes

functions.docs:
Conditional create/replace/delete.

`expected = none` means create only if there is no live record.
`expected = some(version)` requires the current live record to match
exactly. On a mismatch the host returns `applied = false` and the
current entry; it never overwrites the winner. A missing record with an
expected version returns `not-found`.
functions.name: compare-and-swap

functions.docs:
Write a tombstone. The record remains visible to `changes` until the
host's tombstone retention expires.
functions.name: delete

functions.docs: Read one record.
functions.name: get

functions.docs:
Scan one collection in revision order. A cursor from a previous page is
valid until the host reports `stale`.
functions.name: scan

functions.docs:
Create or replace a local record. The host assigns `revision` and
`origin`; the returned entry is authoritative.
functions.name: upsert

types.docs:
Result of a conditional write. On conflict `entry` is the current
authoritative entry, so the caller can re-read and retry.
types.name: cas-result

types.docs:
One stored record. `body` is opaque to the host (JSON, CBOR, or a Spore
schema); `schema` names the body contract.

Local `upsert` ignores `revision` and `origin` and assigns both. Remote
`apply` uses them for last-writer-wins:
  higher `revision` wins; equal revision is broken by lexicographic
  `origin`; a `deleted` entry is a tombstone.
types.name: entry

types.docs:
A record address. `collection` is a Spore-defined namespace
(`email.message`, `chat.message`, `contact`); `id` is stable within it.
types.name: key

types.docs: The exact revision/origin tuple returned by a local write.
types.name: version

packages.name: records

packages.docs:
The scene payload is data, not an interface: it is what `soil:canvas.present`
carries, and it is versioned inside the document so a new node kind never
rebuilds the Spores that draw.

This package exists only so a Spore can ask the host what it accepts before it
builds a document. It deliberately does not describe the document's shape --
that lives in `soil-scene` (Rust) and is checked at present time, where a
producer can be told *why* something was refused.

functions.docs:
Host-enforced ceilings, so a producer can budget against the same numbers
the host will refuse at rather than discovering them by trial.
functions.name: budget

functions.docs:
Highest schema version the host can draw. A producer that needs newer
nodes gets `false` here instead of a failure at present time.
functions.name: supports

packages.name: scene

packages.docs:
Host-composed global search across granted local sources.

This is a derived discovery surface, not authority. Files still come from
`soil:vfs`, records from `soil:records`, and actions from their owning host
capability. A hit is a locator plus display metadata; the caller fetches the
authoritative object through the source capability.

interfaces.docs:
Typed mention resolver for `@` autocomplete.

A candidate is a stable locator, never a copied display name. The caller
inserts `token` into a document/task/record and persists it as a
`mentions` graph link. The host resolves labels and visibility from the
same approved books used by search.

functions.docs:
Resolve a prefix into typed candidates. Empty `kinds` means all supported
kinds. `limit` is host-bounded.
functions.name: suggest

interfaces.name: mentions

types.docs:
A typed graph reference attached to a hit. This is discovery metadata,
not an access grant or a fetched object.
types.name: reference

packages.name: search

packages.docs:
Installed Spore catalog and host-owned launch.

A Spore never scans the filesystem, starts a process, or chooses a window.
The host validates packages, maps them to a launch target, and performs the
launch outside the guest.

functions.docs:
Launch `surface` of `id`.

Fails with `unsupported` when this host cannot present the surface's kind
— a host without a browser view refuses a `web` surface rather than
opening something it cannot render. A name the package does not declare
is `not-found`.
functions.name: launch

types.docs:
One view a package ships, declared so a host can tell what it would have
to provide before it opens anything.

`entry` is a path inside the package, never a content id. The package is
the unit of identity and provenance: its lock and digest already cover
every byte under its root, so a per-asset content id would be a second
version of the same fact and the two would drift.
types.name: surface

types.docs:
How a host presents a surface.

Native rendering is deliberately absent: it is the default, it is what
`[module]` and `[ui]` already are, and a package that needs nothing extra
should not have to declare it.
types.name: surface-kind

packages.name: spore

packages.docs:
Host content-addressed asset cache.

A Spore names a CID, never a path, directory, URL or handle. `read` is
granted by `soil:storage.read` (the default) and `write` by the separate
`soil:storage.write` grant. Writes reach a bounded host cache, never the
asset store or the Spore Store.

functions.docs:
Read the bytes named by a CIDv1 content address.

`max-bytes` bounds the response: an object larger than the limit is
`over-budget`, never a partial payload. `max-bytes == 0` is `invalid`.
functions.name: read

functions.docs:
Commit bytes to the bounded host cache under a CIDv1 address.

Requires `soil:storage.write`; without it the call is `denied`. The host
may refuse an oversized or over-capacity write with `over-budget`. This
never mutates the published asset store.
functions.name: write

packages.name: storage

packages.docs:
Host-owned imported surfaces.

A surface is a native view, remote stream, decoded video, browser view, or
another Spore's render target. The host owns the pixels/texture and composes
them into Canvas. A Spore receives an opaque handle, metadata, damage, and
normalized input only.

types.docs:
Host-owned surface. The host may present, encode, or composite it; the
Spore never receives a texture or native window handle.
types.name: surface

packages.name: surface-import

packages.docs:
Host-rendered terminal surface.

The Spore owns VT parsing (for example with libghostty-vt) and submits a
bounded cell grid. The host owns fonts, shaping, pixels, accessibility and
the input lifecycle. The host never receives raw escape sequences.

Handles are component-instance-scoped. A later revision can replace them
with WIT resources.

functions.docs: Wait for one normalized key or paste. `none` means the timeout elapsed.
functions.name: next-input

functions.docs: Submit a complete frame. Full-frame for v0; damage regions are additive.
functions.name: present

packages.name: terminal

packages.docs:
Host monotonic clock.

Requires the `soil:time` grant. There is no wall clock, timezone, sleep,
timer thread or per-frame callback: a Spore reads elapsed time and waits on
a bounded tick. The host may return a tick earlier than requested, so callers
must re-check their own deadline.

functions.docs:
Monotonic milliseconds from an unspecified host epoch.

Only useful for measuring elapsed time. Values are not comparable across
processes, host restarts or devices.
functions.name: monotonic-ms

functions.docs:
Wait up to `timeout-ms` for the next host tick and return its monotonic
millisecond value. `0` polls without blocking; `none` means the deadline
elapsed. A returned tick may precede the requested deadline.
functions.name: tick

packages.name: time

packages.docs:
Bounded observation and publication on the Unibus.

Unibus L1 routes opaque envelopes; this capability is the Spore-facing edge.
It never exposes credentials, peer identities, or raw sockets. A Spore
subscribes by kind and receives metadata/body bytes; it does not get bus
internals or the ability to bypass grants.

functions.docs:
Poll retained frames for the listed kinds. An empty `kinds` list means
no kinds, never "all"; a Spore must name what it observes.
functions.name: poll

functions.docs:
Publish one frame. Requires `soil:unibus.publish`; destinations and TTL
are bounded by the host. No credentials cross this boundary.
functions.name: publish

packages.name: unibus

packages.docs:
Bounded, explicitly granted VFS mutation.

This is a separate grant from read-only `soil:vfs`. Paths remain canonical
workspace-relative paths; the Spore never receives a host path, descriptor,
provider locator, or raw CID.

functions.docs: Unlink a namespace entry. Content and history are retained.
functions.name: remove

functions.docs: Rename a file. Directory renames are not part of this slice.
functions.name: rename

functions.docs:
Create or replace one file. `expected-version` is the optimistic
concurrency check; `none` means create/replace unconditionally.
functions.name: write

packages.name: vfs-mut

packages.docs:
Read-only VFS namespace.

The Spore names a workspace-relative path, never a host filesystem path,
directory handle, descriptor, URL or CID supplied as authority. The host
canonicalizes the path, enforces the workspace boundary, and applies a
bounded page/range budget. Listing is deterministic by path; sort/search is
`soil:index`'s job.

`read` returns bytes for an already-present object or hydrates a placeholder
through the host's granted content transport. The Spore never chooses the
provider, endpoint, token or lease. A range larger than the host budget is
`over-budget`, never silently truncated.

functions.docs:
List direct children of `parent` in path order.
`parent` empty means the workspace root. `limit` is host-bounded.
functions.name: ls

functions.docs:
Read a bounded byte range. `length == 0` is `invalid`.
The host hydrates a placeholder if its transport grant allows it.
functions.name: read

functions.docs: Fetch one namespace entry without reading its bytes.
functions.name: stat

packages.name: vfs

packages.docs:
Host-owned web/Spore/retained view.

The target is an id in the host's reviewed index, never an arbitrary URL,
path or CID supplied by wasm. The host owns the browser/Spore engine, pixels
and capture buffer; the Spore owns presentation state and normalized actions.

functions.docs: PNG
functions.name: [method]view.close

packages.name: view

packages.docs:
Draft `wasi:audio` proposal, maintained in Soil while no upstream package
exists. This is a bounded PCM sink, not the WebAudio graph API.

functions.docs: Wait until the host queue is empty or the bounded timeout expires.
functions.name: [method]output.drain

functions.docs:
Push interleaved f32 frames. Returns the number of complete frames
accepted; zero means backpressure, not failure.
functions.name: [method]output.write

packages.name: audio
